verdicts.reason: A keeps a sensible left-to-right order (badge, product, headline, CTA), but the NEW pill is cut off at the left edge, the can has lost its cream circle, and the Try It button is jammed against the right edge. B starts with the CTA, which reverses the reading order. Its Try It button is pressed against the left edge and the NEW badge is cropped at the right, so it ends with a stray fragment and the product floats away from the headline.

A puts the CTA first, the button is crammed against the left edge, the subline is squeezed into near-illegible tight text, and the NEW pill collides with the subline under the headline, while the can sits isolated at the far right. B (the same layout as pair 1 A) avoids collisions and keeps the headline and CTA dominant, but its NEW pill is cropped at the left edge, the can's circle is gone and the button touches the right edge.
